title: United Airlines says issue affecting departing flights has been resolved
summary: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a…

image.caption: A United plane is seen at George Bush International Airport in Houston on Saturday. The airline's outage on Monday was the latest in a series of high-profile technology meltdowns. (Ashley Landis/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.
The airline's outage on Monday was the latest high-profile technology meltdown

Chicago-based United said in a statement that while some flights were delayed because of the issue Monday afternoon, flights that were in the air and flights on its United Express regional network were not impacted. It also said, "There is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue."
United apologized to customers for the inconvenience on social media.

Pilots reported to air traffic controllers that the problem was related to United's system that helps them determine a plane's final weight to ensure it can safely take off. United did not immediately provide details about which of the airlines systems were affected.

A recording posted on the ATC app showed a United pilot in Houston asking the tower for permission to stay put at the gate until the system was working again. The app combines live air traffic control radio feeds with real-time visual aircraft tracking.
The flight tracking website FlightAware showed United with 418 delayed flights late Monday afternoon.
The United computer problem is just the latest high-profile technology meltdown.

blocks.text: Earlier in the day, thousands of people reported being unable to access their online accounts at several major U.S. banks after JP Morgan Chase had a technical problem.
On Friday, the FAA ordered every U.S. flight grounded because a new router that was installed malfunctioned and overwhelmed the aging air traffic control system.
And one day earlier, Microsoft experienced a major disruption to its Outlook email service. Microsoft said Saturday that services were fully restored.
